capabilities: Execute code blocks interactively inside notes
Run Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript in local JS/WebAssembly sandboxes
Evaluate other languages via online playgrounds such as Sololearn
Render HTML and CSS using Shadow DOM
Install Python packages like numpy and matplotlib via micropip
extras: Warning in README: only Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript run locally; other languages send source code to third-party websites, so sensitive code may be exposed. README links numpy package list and other docs externally.
problem: Obsidian code blocks are static text; there is no built-in way to execute them and see results inside a note.
summary: Code block runner that executes code interactively in sandboxes like Jupyter notebooks, supporting Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, and others.
